issue.title: [HttpKernel] fixed kernel re-init (when getting unserialized for eg.)
issue.body:
fixes #6254

This was happening to me because in `app/cache/dev/appDevUrlMatcher.php.meta` I have a `Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Config\FileLocator` serialized object, at some point a ConfigCache needs to unserialize this file, when it does, a Kernel gets unserialized too (because this FileLocator class depends on it), and it leads to re-initializing the kernel.

body: This happens to me with a fresh standard edition, if I just remove a semicolon in an action.

I've just tested it again and I don't have the double-display of the error (with a fresh Symfony SE installation), that's really weird. There is a difference between our two setups, but I have no idea which one.

Indeed weird is the right word...

For the record, I'm using PHP 5.4.7 with the built-in web-server (but it also appears with apache) on Ubuntu 12.04.

Related to #6254.

What about a static flag on it so that it gets intialized only once in a process?

body: FYI I also have this on another machine, windows with wampserver 2.2 (php 5.4.3) I haven't tweaked any PHP config, I've kept their default php.ini, I've only enabled some php extensions (gd2 and openssl) through their menu interface.
I can now reproduce this issue but only with the PHP built-in server. I will investigate it further now.

This issue happens because of the Assetic bundle (see https://github.com/symfony/AsseticBundle/blob/master/Routing/AsseticLoader.php#L58). The good news is that is should only happen in the development environment as the route loader should never be used in the production environment.

The issue exists because Assetic is registering a special routing loader, with specific resources that have dependencies on the HttpKernel FileLocator, which in turn needs the Kernel. So, when Symfony serializes the resources for the routing, it serializes the kernel, which is then unserialized to see if all resources are fresh.

I've opened an issue there (see symfony/AsseticBundle#168).
